files.purpose_guess: WRT's own numbered list of the ten records kept at the nursery, in workflow order, with seasonality (living doc or seasonal) and what each is used for.

sheets.name: (document)
sheets.grain: Numbered list item: one record type with description
sheets.notes: Defines the record system: (1) forecasting sheet 3 years ahead (flagged new); (2) seed collecting record (seasonal log including locations); (3) seed records (living doc: seeds collected, tag numbers, treatment, dates sown and pricked); (4) cutting records (living); (5) seed and cutting records by species; (6) seed sowing list (seasonal: what is sown per forecasts, stratification, tray sizes and numbers); (7) pricking out list (seasonal, stage 2; basis of site planting lists; due to the propagation lead each January; 'becomes planting list two seasons later', e.g. pricking out 2024/25 = planting 2026/27); (8) a confirmation count of seedlings pricked out, accounting for deaths; (9) potting on list (seasonal, stage 3; new form each July built from last year's pricking-out list plus the latest propagation stocktake; drives how many seedlings are potted up); (10) nursery stocktake (counts stage 2-4; V150 propagation stocktake; T28/PB3 at least twice a year, confirming plants ready for the next planting season); (11) plant allocation list (stage 4 plants to keystone, community and school sites; one form each spring and autumn); (12) JMN Plant Allocation MASTER (historical record of everything planted, running tally for the trust). Word numbering restarts, so the visible numbers (5 to 10) do not match the record order; counted here as twelve entries. Reports no quantities. Evidence: _Summary of Records JM Nursery.docx › paragraphs 1-43.

files.path: 2. Propagation (cuttings and seeds)/Annual propagation reports/Propagation Report for the year ended December 2024.docx
files.purpose_guess: Propagation lead's narrative report for calendar 2024 plus a January 2025 update, covering pricking-out volumes, tray types, germination, disease and volunteer effort.

sheets.name: (document)
sheets.grain: Narrative sections by date (end-2024 report, 22 January 2025 update)
sheets.notes: Narrative with few figures. Reports over 8,000 seedlings pricked out between late August and the Christmas break, mostly into V150 with some into T28; 915 pricked out on the last nursery day of December 2024. Describes a decision to keep using T28 for flax, better strike rates for small-leaved Olearia (except one species) and frozen Olearia seed sown in August, damping off in two tray batches (a Coprosma and Plagianthus), regular fungicide spraying of Veronica/Hebe, seed collecting starting for Coprosma, doubt over beech seed, and seedling mix from one commercial supplier. Weeding suffered from the push on numbers. Names volunteers and the author (names not copied). Evidence: Propagation Report for the year ended December 2024.docx › paragraphs 1-15. The 8,000 total is a rounded text figure and can be compared with the weekly pricking-out logs and the 2024/25 pricking-out list.

quality_issues.issue: Totals are stated as prose ('over 8000'), not as a table, so they cannot be tied to workbook totals without calculation.

quality_issues.issue: Names of volunteers appear in the text (not reproduced).

files.path: 2. Propagation (cuttings and seeds)/Annual propagation reports/Annual Propagation summary April 2021.docx
files.purpose_guess: Propagation lead's annual summary for April 2021 to March 2022: seed supply, cuttings, potting mix, trays (including the first T28 trial), volunteers, plant health and target performance.

sheets.name: (document)
sheets.grain: Narrative sections by theme (seed, cuttings, mix, trays, volunteers, health, targets)
sheets.notes: Narrative, no tables and almost no numeric totals. Key process facts: seed of dependable species was collected, cleaned and stored; insect damage to seed worse than usual; beech produced little viable seed; wind-borne seed is sown when ripe (summer/autumn), most other seed sown early August; pricking out began too early when seedlings were too small; cuttings are used for species with poor seed (Corokia, totara, Hebe, Carmichaelia, Ozothamnus); T28 trays (donated, ~500 ml mix, about double the capacity of 35F trays, V150 holds 150 ml) were trialled for manuka, Carex and Poa cita, giving plants ready a season earlier than via V150 to PB3, with flax, cabbage trees and beech to be trialled next; the author notes T28 use disturbs the stocktake numbers kept by the stocktaker; aspirational targets were met except Corokia cotoneaster, Olearia lineata and Olearia odorata; soil mix and acidity affected Olearia losses. Evidence: Annual Propagation summary April 2021.docx › paragraphs 1-44. It is the earliest written explanation of why T28 exists as a pathway.

quality_issues.issue: File name says 'April 2021' but the content covers April 2021 to March 2022 and is signed April 2022; related versions exist in the same folder (Propagation Report March 2022, Jan 22, April 2022, and a copy), not read here.
